summary: This work presents a traveling-wave parametric amplifier with integrated on-chip input and output diplexers for pump delivery and routing, eliminating external microwave components. The device achieves 13 dB broadband gain across 2 GHz (6–8 GHz signal band) with average system-added noise of 2 quanta, as measured by shot-noise tunnel junction calibration.
motivation: Conventional TWPAs require off-chip directional couplers and diplexers for pump injection and filtering, adding loss, complexity, and limiting scalability in multiplexed superconducting-circuit readout architectures.
method: A four-wave-mixing Josephson TWPA with niobium trilayer junctions ($I_c \approx 5$ µA) and integrated fifth-order Chebyshev diplexers (crossover at 8.5 GHz, footprint ~300 µm × 300 µm) were co-fabricated on a single chip using amorphous-silicon-dielectric capacitors ($\tan \delta \approx 4 \times 10^{-4}$). The diplexers separate signal and idler paths, with a phase-matching resonator at 8.7 GHz inserted periodically in the shunt branch.
result: At optimized pump power (−76.8 dBm at the TWPA input, 9.06 GHz), the device delivers 13 dB gain with a minimum chain-added noise of 2 quanta between 6–8 GHz; isolating the TWPA contribution yields $N_{\mathrm{TWPA}} = 1.17 \pm 0.14$ quanta at 7.74 GHz.
